te: Working group proposes an outline for a study of counter-drone systems, and the space study visit summarised
se: The meeting noted the concept for a study of counter-drone systems, covering types of threat, technology and cooperation with industry, and noted the summary of the study visit to the Royal Thai Air Force Space Operations Center and GISTDA, which is developing a constellation of 18 satellites, and proposed that researchers from the armed forces take part in the design
it: Concept and outline of the study of counter-drone systems
Summary of the study visit to the Royal Thai Air Force Space Operations Center and GISTDA

te: Approaches to procuring weapons in emergencies followed up, and the subcommittee's working manual
se: The meeting followed up progress on proposals for procuring weapons and military equipment in combat or emergency situations in a way that is flexible, transparent and lawful, noting that the Public Procurement and Supplies Administration Act B.E. 2560 (2017) allows the specific method of procurement to be used, and considered the subcommittee's working manual
it: Progress on proposals for approaches to procuring weapons and military equipment in combat or emergency situations
The subcommittee's working manual

te: Defence industry proposals heard, and approval sought for a study visit on space
se: The meeting invited the President of the Defence Industry Association and private sector representatives to give information on approaches to procuring weapons and military equipment in combat or emergency situations and on the problems of Thai businesses. They proposed improving some laws and setting conditions for technology transfer in procurement. The meeting set up a working group on law to study this, and sought approval for a trip to the Royal Thai Air Force Space Operations Center and GISTDA
it: Recommendations of the Defence Industry Association on approaches to procuring weapons and military equipment in combat or emergency situations
Approval sought for a trip to the Royal Thai Air Force Space Operations Center and GISTDA

te: The Pha Muang and Naresuan Task Forces to be heard on boundaries and security along the border
se: Meeting on Wednesday 18 November 2026 at 09.00, Committee Meeting Room CA 327, floor 3, Parliament House. Agenda: problems and solutions concerning boundaries and the security situation along Thailand's borders with neighbouring countries, with the Commander of the Pha Muang Task Force and the Commander of the Naresuan Task Force, or their representatives, invited. (The Senate has not yet published the summary of this meeting, so this text is the agenda from the meeting notice, not the meeting's resolutions.)
it: Problems and solutions concerning boundaries and the security situation along the border

te: Pre-meeting video · The Pha Muang and Naresuan Task Forces to be heard on boundaries and security along the border
The Surasakmontri and Suranaree Task Forces heard on the Mekong border and the northeastern border
se: The meeting invited the Commander of the Surasakmontri Task Force and the Commander of the Suranaree Task Force to give information, for example on the Thai–Lao border along the Mekong River in 5 provinces, where water levels fluctuate with the operation of dams upstream, causing riverbank erosion and making river patrols difficult in the dry season, as well as on the suppression of drugs and crime. The meeting noted the information
it: Situation on the Thai–Lao border along the Mekong River (Surasakmontri Task Force)
Border situation in the area of responsibility of the Suranaree Task Force

te: Meeting summary video · The Surasakmontri and Suranaree Task Forces heard on the Mekong border and the northeastern border
Pre-meeting video · The Surasakmontri and Suranaree Task Forces heard on the Mekong border and the northeastern border
The Burapha and Surasi Task Forces heard on the border situation
se: The meeting invited the Commander of the Burapha Task Force and the Commander of the Surasi Task Force to give information on the security situation along the border, such as the situation on the Thai–Cambodian border, the care of boundary markers, the smuggling of workers and illegal goods, threats from call-centre gangs, and people's farmland. The meeting noted the information
it: Security situation along the border (Burapha Task Force and Surasi Task Force)

te: Meeting summary video · The Burapha and Surasi Task Forces heard on the border situation
A 6-part framework set for studying foreign nationals who may affect security
se: The meeting approved a 6-part framework for studying law enforcement concerning foreign nationals at risk of breaking laws in ways that affect internal security: geopolitics, land holding through nominees, control of buildings and places of worship, immigration and overstaying, and social and cultural conflict, adding the dimensions of education and border crossings. The secretariat plans to invite 13 agencies to clarify on 12 and 19 November 2026, and is preparing a plan for site visits in January
it: 6-part framework for studying foreign nationals who may affect internal security
Plan to invite 13 agencies to clarify on 12 and 19 November 2026, and plan for site visits

te: Meeting summary video · A 6-part framework set for studying foreign nationals who may affect security
Work plan for fiscal year 2027: 7 matters taken on, and 8 border forces to be invited
se: The meeting considered its work plan for fiscal year 2027, including continuing work and 7 matters referred by the committee. It approved inviting the commanders of border forces, such as the Burapha, Surasi, Surasakmontri, Suranaree, Pha Muang, Naresuan and Thepsatri Task Forces and the Chanthaburi and Trat Border Defence Command, to give information, and appointed 28 advisers for fiscal year 2027
it: Work plan for fiscal year 2027, and matters referred by the committee
Commanders of border forces invited to give information on border security
Appointment of advisers to the subcommittee for fiscal year 2027

te: Meeting summary video · Work plan for fiscal year 2027: 7 matters taken on, and 8 border forces to be invited
Draft report on the study of the internal security law approved for submission to the committee and the Senate
se: The meeting approved the draft report on the study of the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008) for submission to the committee and then the Senate, approved the video and statement on its work in fiscal year 2026, and took up for study the situation of the arrival of certain groups of foreign nationals that may affect security and public order
it: Draft report on the study of the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)
Video and statement on the work done in fiscal year 2026
The situation of the arrival of certain groups of foreign nationals that may affect security

te: Report on the academic forum approved, and the 2026 annual report prepared
se: The meeting approved the summary report of the academic forum "Sustainable Internal Security Management: The Role and Direction of the Internal Security Operations Command in an Integrated Dimension", held on 26 August 2026, and assigned subcommittee members and the secretary to prepare a summary report for 2026 for the meeting on 22 September 2026
it: Summary report of the academic forum, 26 August 2026
Preparation of the summary report for 2026
